value_chain_report.bottleneck_analysis: Mobile operating systems (Apple iOS, Google Android) and AI component suppliers (Nvidia) are the critical bottlenecks. Apple controls app distribution and data tracking signals, which previously caused ad signal loss. Nvidia controls the GPU market for AI training. If Nvidia raises prices, Meta's capital expenditures increase significantly, though Meta's massive free cash flow and custom silicon development (MTIA) provide a buffer against long-term value leak.
value_chain_report.top_substitutes: 1. TikTok (short-form video), 2. YouTube (video/entertainment), 3. iMessage/Snapchat (messaging). Realistic switching scenario: Younger demographics completely migrate daily screen time to TikTok for entertainment, forcing advertisers to shift budgets away from Instagram and Facebook to maintain target audience reach.
value_chain_report.pricing_power_assessment: Meta uses an auction-based pricing model for digital advertising. Because of its massive reach and AI-driven ad targeting (Advantage+), it delivers high return on ad spend (ROAS). This allows Meta to naturally drive up average cost-per-mille (CPM) and pass costs to advertisers, as evidenced by expanding gross margins and continuous revenue growth despite previous iOS signal loss.
value_chain_report.analysis_summary: Meta possesses dominant strategic leverage driven by unparalleled network effects across its Family of Apps (over 3 billion daily active people). Buyer power is low due to a highly fragmented advertiser base reliant on Meta's targeting algorithms. Substitution risk is moderate but actively mitigated by aggressive product adaptation (e.g., Reels). The main vulnerability lies in supplier power, specifically reliance on mobile OS gatekeepers (Apple/Google) and AI hardware monopolies (Nvidia). Despite these bottlenecks, Meta's pricing power and massive cash generation secure its position as a dominant platform.
